previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of Type 1 diabetes and gastroparesis was admitted for severe nausea and vomiting, consistent with a gastroparesis flare. She had elevated blood glucose levels and required IV fluids and medication adjustments. A chest X-ray revealed a small left lower lobe pneumonia, likely due to aspiration from vomiting, and she was treated with levofloxacin and metronidazole. An EGD with Botox injection was performed, after which her symptoms improved and she advanced to a soft diet. Her blood pressure, initially elevated, normalized with treatment. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete her antibiotic course, continue adjusted insulin therapy, and follow up with gastroenterology and endocrinology. Iron deficiency anemia was noted and recommended for outpatient monitoring.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ woman with a history of type I DM, 
gastroparesis, and HTN who is admitted to the ICU with DKA on an 
insulin drip.
  
# DKA:  Unclear trigger, though unclear how compliant patient 
has been with her medications.  MI was ruled out with negative 
enzymes and UA and CXR were all negative for acute infectious 
process. Insulin drip downtitrated with improvement in blood 
sugars and she was transitioned to subcutaneous insulin. She was 
given 15 units lantus in pm on ___, 15 units in am on ___ 
and her usual 30 units on ___ in pm. Her anion gap remained 
closed and she tolerated several meals on ___ without further 
nausea or vomiting. Blood sugars prior to discharge ranged 
100-200s.  
  
# GASTROPARESIS:  Patient has failed multiple treatment 
modalities for gastroparesis.  Appears as though she has minimal 
benefit from botox injections in past. Nausea was improved on 
___ and she was toelrating a diet so GI was not consulted. She 
was treated symptomatically with anti-emetics. 
  
# EMESIS: Upon arrival to the MICU, patient had continued 
retching and emesis.  There was ? flecks of coffee ground 
material in emesis basin from dried blood likely from known 
severe esophagitis and irritation.  Patient remained 
hemodynamically stable. HCT trended down but she was likely 
hemconcentrated on admission and it was not far from baseline. 
She was treated with IV PPI which was changed to PO when 
tolerating POs. 

#?UTI: urine sample concerning for UTI and she was started on 
cipro.  Repeat UA was unconcerning for infection and antibiotics 
were discontinued.  She denied dysuria on discharge

# HTN:  Initially held home antihypertensives but then restarted 
on ___. 
  
# DMI:  Continued Lantus 30units QHS and humalog sliding scale 
once gap has closed.
